section_summary: This section contains the concluding portions of an initial copy and the substantial part of a duplicate copy of Tokyo Embassy Despatch No. 5321 (January 23, 1941), transmitting Report No. 1671 on conditions in Japan during December 1940, along with monthly schedules of telegrams and despatches. The report surveys Japanese-American tensions over trade restrictions and rights in China, Foreign Minister Matsuoka's address to the America-Japan Society, relations with Great Britain, China, French Indochina, Thailand, the Netherlands East Indies, Russia, and Germany, as well as Cabinet reorganization and the establishment of the New National Structure. It also details Japan's economic and financial conditions for 1940, including trade controls, agricultural production declines, and wartime industrial adjustments.

subfiles.about: Concluding portion of a duplicate copy of Tokyo Embassy Despatch No. 5321, containing Section VI of Report No. 1671 on economic conditions and appended monthly lists of telegrams and despatches.
subfiles.summary: This subfile contains the concluding pages of Report No. 1671 on conditions in Japan during December 1940, focusing on national economic and financial conditions for the year 1940. It assesses agricultural shortfalls in rice and cocoon harvests, raw material shortages in heavy industries, export distribution regulations, and foreign trade balances within the yen bloc and with foreign-currency nations. The report is followed by a complete schedule of 145 telegrams sent from Tokyo to the Department of State in December 1940 covering diplomatic and administrative matters. It concludes with a chronological list of 79 despatches forwarded to Washington during the same month.
subfiles.title: Report of Conditions in Japan During the Month of December 1940 (Report No. 1671, duplicate copy)

subfiles.about: Tokyo Embassy Despatch No. 5321 transmitting Report No. 1671 on political, diplomatic, and economic conditions in Japan during December 1940, accompanied by a list of telegrams.
subfiles.summary: Ambassador Joseph C. Grew transmits the Embassy's monthly report for December 1940 pursuant to Department instructions. The report reviews strained Japanese-American relations, Matsuoka's address at the America-Japan Society and Grew's response, Japanese replies to protests regarding infractions of American rights in China, and Nomura's delayed mission. It surveys Japan's foreign relations with Great Britain, the Nanking regime under Wang Ching-wei, the Thailand-Indochina border dispute, trade missions in the Netherlands East Indies, and relations with the Soviet Union, Germany, and Italy. In domestic affairs, it analyzes Konoe's Cabinet reorganization, the Imperial Rule Assistance Association, civil service reform, and the New Economic Structure outline, followed by financial and trade statistics for 1940 and an appended list of December telegrams.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 5321, transmitting Report No. 1671: Report of Conditions in Japan During the Month of December 1940
